data.title: Project Santa Fe Foundation Expands Leadership With Three Distinguished New Board Members to Advance Predictive, Value-Based Laboratory Medicine
data.description:
Project Santa Fe Foundation Expands Leadership With Three Distinguished New Board Members to Advance Predictive, Value-Based Laboratory Medicine

Project Santa Fe Foundation (PSFF) and Clinical Lab 2.0 (CL2.0) are pleased to welcome three distinguished leaders to the Board of Directors. They each bring deep expertise to advance the global movement of transitioning laboratories from reactive confirmation of diagnosis to proactive prediction using risk stratification of data the lab already possesses.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827780303/en/

Pictured left to right: Mercè Jordà, MD, PhD, MBA, Chair, Pathology & Laboratory Medicine, University of Miami Miller School of Medicine; William G. Morice, MD, PhD, President & CEO, Mayo Collaborative Services/Mayo Clinic Laboratories; Peter Weir, MD, MPH, Chief Population Health Officer, University of Utah Health

Dr. Jordà possesses over 25 years of academic and consultative pathology leadership focused on cancer care, Dr. Morice has contributed decades of hematopathology expertise and national leadership, and Dr. Weir offers a physician's perspective on value-based care and population health strategy. Together, these leaders strengthen our mission to build the evidence base for laboratory-driven, value-based, patient-centered care.

When asked about his decision to join the PSFF Board, Dr. Morice thoughtfully replied, “Throughout my career in laboratory medicine and pathology, I’ve seen the value our profession creates for the entire healthcare community. However, for that value to be recognized, fostered, and rewarded, we must leverage our domain knowledge and develop transformational models for both clinical delivery and reimbursement. That is why I am so humbled and delighted to join the PSFF board and [to] have the opportunity to contribute to the pursuit of its mission.”

Dr. Weir added, “A lot of my career has centered on finding better ways to use clinical data to improve care at the population level. The work Project Santa Fe [Foundation] is doing aligns closely with the questions I’ve been working on for years, and I’m looking forward to contributing where I can.”

Please join us in formally celebrating these trailblazers joining the PSFF and CL2.0 team!

Contact us:
Project Sante Fe Foundation and Clinical Lab 2.0 (a Project Santa Fe Foundation initiative)
https://cl2lab.org/
email: info@cl2lab.org

data.title: ICE Review: Canola Declines Ahead of Long Weekend
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures closed lower on Friday, pressured by declines in the Chicago soy complex.

While crude oil was mixed and offered little direction to the vegetable oils, there were gains in most European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil contracts.

Saskatchewan reported its canola harvest was four per cent complete and yielding 38 bushels per acre. Alberta is set to issue its crop report later this afternoon.

The Canadian Grain Commission said canola exports for the week ended Aug. 30 fell to 58,300 tonnes from 118,100 the previous week. Cumulative exports reached 584,800 tonnes compared to 482,300 a year ago.

An analyst said it's quite typical for this time of year for exports to slow ahead of harvest.

The CGC said domestic use of canola rose to 294,600 tonnes from 267,300 the week before. The year-to-date was nearly 1.07 million tonnes versus 893,000 this time last year.

Statistics Canada is scheduled to release its stocks of principal crops on Sept. 8. That will be followed by StatCan's production report on Sept. 16.

India was projected to produce slightly more rapeseed in 2026-27.

The United States Department of Agriculture attaché in New Delhi estimated the next crop at 12.1 million tonnes versus 11.9 million in 2025-26.

The Canadian dollar was weaker on Friday afternoon, with the loonie at 72.25 U.S. cents, compared to Thursday's close of 72.52.

The markets in Canada and the United States will be closed on Monday for Labour Day.

There were 39,575 canola contracts traded on Friday, compared to 50,674 on Thursday. Spreading accounted for 21,590 contracts traded.

data.title: CauzzyAI and Unilever Prestige Partner to Accelerate AI Innovation Across Prestige Beauty
data.description:
CauzzyAI and Unilever Prestige Partner to Accelerate AI Innovation Across Prestige Beauty

CauzzyAI (cauzzy.ai) today announced a strategic partnership with Unilever Prestige, bringing its Enterprise AI platform within the Unilever Prestige portfolio. The collaboration marks a significant milestone in Unilever Prestige's vision to become an AI-native enterprise, embedding intelligent AI into everyday business operations to accelerate innovation, simplify complex processes, and enable teams to make faster, more informed decisions.

As AI reshapes the future of consumer goods, Unilever Prestige is moving beyond experimentation to enterprise-wide transformation. Through CauzzyAI's enterprise AI platform, participating brands will leverage intelligent “AI Agents” that securely connect across ERP systems (Oracle NetSuite), enterprise data warehouses, and other critical business applications to automate complex workflows, generate real-time business insights, and help teams focus on higher-value work that drives growth and innovation.

The partnership is designed to create measurable impact across finance, operations, supply chain, commercial planning, and executive decision-making by simplifying access to enterprise knowledge, accelerating business processes, and enabling smarter, data-driven decisions across the organization. Rather than introducing another AI tool, the collaboration embeds AI into the core of how work gets done, connecting data across business systems, eliminating repetitive manual tasks, and empowering employees to spend more time innovating, solving complex challenges, and delivering exceptional consumer experiences. The initiative represents another important step in Unilever Prestige's broader technology strategy to integrate AI into the fabric of the business, transforming artificial intelligence from a productivity enhancer into a strategic capability that drives innovation, operational excellence, and long-term competitive advantage.

“The companies that lead the next decade won't simply adopt AI, they'll redesign how they innovate around it,” said Narayan Parasuraman, CIO, Unilever Prestige. “Our ambition is to embed intelligence into every layer of the business, giving our teams immediate access to insights, automating complexity behind the scenes, and enabling faster, more confident decisions. AI isn't just another technology capability; it's becoming a catalyst for how modern organizations innovate, collaborate, and grow.”

“For years we've optimized workflows. Now we're reimagining how work happens,” said MC Gasco Busson, CEO of Unilever Prestige. “When AI can reason across our enterprise data, connect information that previously lived in silos, and simplify complex processes, our people can spend more time solving meaningful business challenges, creating exceptional consumer experiences, and accelerating innovation across our portfolio. That's where the real competitive advantage lies.”

Unlike traditional AI assistants that respond to individual prompts, CauzzyAI’s “AI Agents” are designed to understand business context, orchestrate complex workflows across multiple enterprise systems, and continuously surface insights that help organizations operate with greater speed, intelligence, and agility.

“We're entering an era where AI becomes part of every business decision, every operational process, and every innovation cycle,” said Josh LaSov, Co-Founder and CEO of CauzzyAI. “The organizations that embrace this shift first won't simply become more efficient, they'll become more adaptive, more intelligent, and better equipped to innovate at scale. Unilever Prestige recognizes that AI is evolving from a productivity tool into a foundational business capability.

“This partnership validates a new generation of enterprise AI,” LaSov continued. “We're building AI that understands how businesses operate, connects knowledge across the enterprise, and helps people move from information to action in seconds.”

As leading consumer brands increasingly invest in generative AI to transform product innovation, customer engagement, and enterprise operations, Unilever Prestige is taking a broader approach by embedding AI across the organization to create a more intelligent, agile, and connected business. Together, Unilever Prestige and CauzzyAI are demonstrating how enterprise AI can unlock meaningful business outcomes while empowering people to innovate faster, simplify complexity, and shape the future of prestige beauty.

data.title: We're in our 60s. We earn $345,000 and have $1 million in 403(b)s. Is it too late for Roth conversions?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Roth assets would provide our children with tax-free distributions'

"Upon either of us passing away, the surviving spouse will receive 100% of the deceased spouse's pension." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm 66, retired, and receive a pension of $165,000 a year, with a 2% annual COLA. I currently have about $450,000 in a 403(b) and $35,000 in a Roth IRA.

My wife is 61 and plans to retire in January 2027. Her projected pension will be $180,000 a year, also with a 2% annual COLA. She has $470,000 in a 403(b) and $6,000 in a Roth IRA.

Once she retires, our combined pension income will be $345,000 a year before any withdrawals from our retirement accounts. Both pensions should continue increasing by 2% annually.

In addition, upon either of us passing away, the surviving spouse will receive 100% of the deceased spouse's pension.

Together, we have nearly $1 million in tax-deferred 403(b) accounts, compared with only about $41,000 in Roth accounts. We also anticipate receiving an inheritance of $600,000.

Depending on how the inheritance is structured, some of those funds could potentially be used to pay the income taxes associated with Roth conversions.

Given our relatively high level of guaranteed pension income, does it actually make sense for us to pursue Roth conversions?

More specifically, would our situation favor:

-- Aggressively converting a substantial portion of our 403(b) accounts to Roth accounts while we are still relatively young;

-- Making smaller, strategic Roth conversions over several years to manage our tax brackets and Medicare IRMAA exposure; or

-- Simply leaving the tax-deferred accounts alone and accepting the future RMDs and associated taxes?

I'm particularly interested in understanding the trade-off between paying taxes today at what may already be a relatively high marginal rate vs. potentially paying higher taxes later.

There is also an estate-planning consideration: Roth assets would provide our children with tax-free distributions, whereas traditional retirement accounts could create a tax burden.

In other words, when a couple already has more than $345,000 a year of lifetime pension income, is a Roth conversion still worth pursuing?

To Roth or Not To Roth

Don't miss: 'My main goal is to help people': I'm single, 74, with $10 million burning a hole in my pocket. What should I do?

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

At this point in your life - even taking your children's inheritance into account - it may be more trouble than it's worth.

Dear Roth,

It's a calculation that should be made with a CFP, but my gut tells me that the window for Roth conversions has narrowed, meaning very piecemeal conversions.

An aggressive conversion strategy probably isn't justified given your wealth and income, but a multi-year Roth-conversion strategy deserves at least some consideration.

You are 66, so the traditional-account RMD clock isn't an immediate crisis. Under current rules, your traditional retirement-plan RMDs won't happen for another few years.

You could convert a modest portion of your traditional 403(b) accounts each year if it keeps you in the same tax bracket and prevents you from tipping over into higher Medicare premiums.

The best time to make such conversions, if you decide to do so, is later in the year when you know exactly how much income you have during the tax year, or during a market downturn.

A multi-year Roth-conversion strategy deserves attention.

A Roth conversion would likely be more attractive if you are currently living in a relatively low or, better yet, zero income-tax state and expect to move to a higher-tax state in the future.

It may be inevitable that your heirs face significant taxes. The SECURE Act forces most non-spouse heirs to empty an inherited traditional IRA within 10 years.

Using some of your $600,000 inheritance to pay tax on Roth conversions can be quite a bit more attractive than funding the tax from your 403(b) accounts.

And, yes, your Medicare premiums, which are in part based on your income, are typically a big consideration when deciding whether to make Roth conversions.

Related: We have $8 million in traditional IRAs. Should we tap them to buy a house - and take the tax hit?

High Medicare premiums

You will already be paying a high premium. Here's why: For 2026, married couples filing jointly begin paying IRMAA above $218,000 of MAGI.

But the higher tiers are $274,000, $342,000, $410,000 and $750,000. Above $410,000, Part B premium is $649.20 a month per person vs. $202.90 at the standard level.

Eligibility for your ACA health-insurance subsidies and IRMAA surcharges is based on your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI).

Withdrawals from traditional IRAs and 401(k)s, capital gains and dividends count as taxable income, while qualified withdrawals from Roth accounts don't count toward MAGI.

IRMAA surcharges are based on your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) from two years prior; the income data used to calculate your Medicare premiums at that time.

You can only avoid or reduce surcharges if the gain resulted from a "life-changing event," such as retirement or death of a spouse, according to the Social Security Administration.

Don't miss: 'I'm leaving money on the table': I'm 64 and my husband is 70. Should I take spousal benefits or wait for my own?

An enviable position

Your $345,000 in annual pension income puts you in an unusual, if enviable position. I asked Wes Karger, co-founder and managing partner at TwinFocus, about your predicament.

Your dilemma is less about whether you need Roth assets to fund your retirement, and more about whether converting some of those assets can improve your long-term tax position.

He is cautious about a conversion. "There is an opportunity cost associated with paying that tax today rather than allowing those assets to remain invested on a tax-deferred basis," he says.

Karger points out another important consideration not addressed in your question: your investment strategy and expected return profile of your retirement assets.

You could end up paying a relatively high marginal tax rate to convert assets into a Roth, only to experience a significant market decline due to an unforeseen economic or geopolitical event.

You don't need Roth assets to fund your retirement.

He would evaluate your decision in the context of your underlying investment portfolio, expected returns, volatility, and overall balance sheet, not simply based on the size of their 403(b)s.

"We would, therefore, generally lean toward smaller, deliberate conversions over a number of years rather than an aggressive conversion program," Karger says. (If not small, strategic.)

This approach provides you with flexibility to evaluate your circumstances every year, and also "avoids making a large, irreversible tax decision based on a single year's circumstances."

Finally, your Social Security may not be the deciding factor, given your other assets and income, but it's worth mentioning and including in your retirement stress test.

It's never too late to make these decisions. Well, to be honest, it can be too late! But you still have some time left before those all-important RMDs kick in.

Don't miss: 'The estrangement isn't about politics': My daughter hasn't spoken to me for 4 years. Do I leave her a monthly annuity?

BENSALEM, Pa., Sept. 4, 2026

BENSALEM, Pa., Sept. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith announces that investors with substantial losses have opportunity to lead the securities fraud class action lawsuit against York Space Systems, Inc.

IF YOU ARE AN INVESTOR WHO SUFFERED A LOSS IN YORK SPACE SYSTEMS, INC. (YSS), CONTACT THE LAW OFFICES OF HOWARD G. SMITH BEFORE OCTOBER 30, 2026 (LEAD PLAINTIFF DEADLINE) TO PARTICIPATE IN THE ONGOING SECURITIES FRAUD LAWSUIT.

Contact the Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to discuss your legal rights by email at howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, by telephone at (215) 638-4847 or visit our website at www.howardsmithlaw.com.

What Is The Lawsuit About?
The complaint filed in this class action alleges that Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) that York's onboard mission and payload software was not fully functional before satellites were launched; (2) that this ongoing trend presented a risk to the Company's contracts with the SDA, deceived the SDA with false advertising to win its contracts, cut corners, and delivered satellites whose mission-critical-software was not completed; and (3) that, as a result of the foregoing, Defendants' positive statements about the Company's business, operations, and prospects, were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

data.title: Credit Bureau, Fair Isaac Shares Retreat as FHFA Chief Pulte Slams Industry — Update
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall 




  Shares of major credit bureaus and Fair Isaac fell after a top federal housing regulator criticized their prices and the reliance on FICO scores in mortgage lending. 



  Shares of Fair Isaac, the company behind the FICO score, were down 18% to $922.67 in Friday morning trading. Equifax's stock was off 7.9% at $174.26, TransUnion was down 8% at $78.09, and shares in Experian retreated 4.8% to $37.91 in over-the-counter trading. 



  Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte took to X on Thursday night to accuse Fair Isaac of operating a monopoly over credit scores. He said he was directing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to approve all lenders using the rival VantageScore model. 



  The agency had previously greenlit the use of VantageScore 4.0 last summer, according to The Wall Street Journal. 



  "FICO supports Director Pulte's commitment to foster a competitive environment that is based on performance, trusted analytics, and outcomes for borrowers, lenders, and investors," the company said in a Friday statement. 



  It added that its FICO Score 10T is the most predictive credit score available and is expected to be widely implemented across the market. 



  Pulte also accused the three credit bureaus--Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion--of "overcharging Americans for far too long" and stringing along regulators. 



  "We are seriously considering bi-merge, and stronger solutions (SAFER and SOUNDER)," Pulte wrote in one post. "We will not allow companies to take advantage of American consumers." 



  The three credit bureaus named by Pulte did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 



  "We have asked the CEOs of the Credit Bureaus for solutions but they seem more intent on "happy talk", tapping us along with meetings, and operating as "cartel-like", which is not in the best interest of American homeowners," Pulte said in another post. "Time for a change." 





  Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com
